question: Which of the following classical dance forms from southern India derives its textual sanction from 'Balarama Bharatam' and 'Hastalakshana Deepika'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical dance-drama form that originated in Kerala, India, and is renowned for its elaborate costumes, face painting, and expressive gestures.
 
• The textual foundation of Kathakali is derived from two ancient treatises: **'Balarama Bharatam'**, which focuses on classical dance and drama, and **'Hastalakshana Deepika'**, which explains the gestures and hand movements.
 
• Kathakali combines elements of dance, music, and acting, rooted in themes from **Indian epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana**.
 
• The art form employs intricate facial expressions and a vocabulary of hand gestures called **mudras**, which are codified in the 'Hastalakshana Deepika'.
 
• Kathakali is performed traditionally as a temple art and later evolved into a theatrical art form performed in open-air theatres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Balarama Bharatam**: An ancient Sanskrit text attributed to Karthika Thirunal Balarama Varma, focusing on the theory and practice of natya (drama) and nritya (dance).
 
• **Hastalakshana Deepika**: A seminal treatise that codifies the hand gestures or mudras used in Kathakali and other traditional Indian dance forms.
 
• **Costume and Makeup**: Kathakali performers wear intricate and colorful costumes, including large headdresses, and apply elaborate facial makeup to depict various characters like gods, demons, and humans.
 
• **Musical Accompaniment**: The performance is accompanied by traditional percussion instruments like the **chenda** and **maddalam**, along with vocalists narrating the story.
 
• **Training and Rigorous Practice**: Kathakali artists undergo years of intense training, focusing on body flexibility, facial expressions, and synchronization of gestures with music and rhythm.
